data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'kapi', meaning 'hair' or 'black'. Kapil is a name of Lord Shiva, who is depicted as having dark, matted hair. The name Kapil carries the meaning “Black-haired, dark complexioned” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kapil usually hope their child will grow to embody black-haired, dark complexioned and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kapil holds great significance in Hindu culture. Kapil is not just a personal name, but also the name of one of the seven Rishis or sages in Hindu mythology. Kapil Muni, also known as Maharishi Kapil, is considered to be the founder of the ancient Indian Tradition of Yoga. Kapil is recalled in various Hindu scriptures including the Mahabharata, where he is portrayed as imparting wisdom to King Yudhishthira. The name Kapil is also associated with Lord Shiva, one of the three major Hindu deities and is believed to constantly meditate on Mount Kailash.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Kapil lies in its connection to Lord Shiva and the ancient Indian Tradition of Yoga. The sound and vibration of the name Kapil are believed to connect the individual to the divine consciousness of Lord Shiva, helping one to attain inner peace, self-realization, and spiritual growth. Kapil is also a reminder of the importance of wisdom and learning in one's spiritual journey. The name evokes images of meditation, self-realization, and enlightenment, inspiring individuals to seek knowledge, self-discipline, and inner peace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Kapil in Sanskrit means 'those with the dark complexion like the ripened corn.' It is also symbolic of the sage Kapila, an incarnation of Lord Shiva, who imparted knowledge to the sage Nachiketa and enlightened him on the nature of death.

vedic_reference.note: Kapil is a name of Lord Shiva and Sage Kapila.

historical_references.reference: The sage Kapil Muni, also known as Kashyapa or Kapila, is considered the founder of the Sankhya philosophy, one of the six major Indian philosophies. He is believed to have lived in the 7th or 8th century BC.

According to Hindu mythology, the sage Kapil is the guru of the great sage Vyasa, who authored the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita. Kapil is believed to have imparted the knowledge of the Samkhya philosophy to Vyasa.
